In **ascending order,** the $x$-coordinates of the points where the hyperbola $14{x}^{2}-5{y}^{2}=64$ intersects the line $y=\sqrt{2}x$ are

$\,x=$
{{field-1}}$\,$ and $\,x=$
{{field-2}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the points where the hyperbola intersects the line $y=\sqrt{2}x,$ we first replace $y$ with $\sqrt{2}x$ in the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}14{x}^{2}-5{y}^{2} & =64 \\ 14{x}^{2}-5(\sqrt{2}x)^{2} & =64 \\ 14{x}^{2}-5(2{x}^{2}) & =64 \\ 14{x}^{2}-10{x}^{2} & =64 \\ 4{x}^{2} & =64 \\ {x}^{2} & =16 \\ x & =\pm 4\end{aligned}
$$

So, in ascending order, the $x$-coordinates of the points of intersection are
$x=-4$ and $x=4.$
